name: Grażynacore
summary: Grażynacore is an ironic term describing the visual style of glitter graphics shared predominantly by Polish women around 60 years of age on social media platforms, particularly Facebook.
description:
Grażynacore is an ironic term describing the visual style of glitter graphics shared predominantly by Polish women around 60 years of age on social media platforms, particularly Facebook. [ 1 ]

The style is saturated with kitsch sentimentality, drawing on visual conventions that stretch back to socialist-era sound postcards and the cassette culture of 1990s Disco Polo . Though the term is applied ironically by younger Polish internet users, the graphics themselves are produced and circulated in complete earnest by their primary audience, giving Grażynacore a dual existence as both a genuine internet visual tradition and a subject of affectionate parody.

The name derives from "Grażyna," a Polish given name strongly associated with women born in the mid-20th century. Unlike most Polish names, which are borrowed from Latin or Slavic tradition, Grażyna was coined entirely by the Romantic poet Adam Mickiewicz for his 1823 narrative poem of the same name. [ 1 ] Its association with a specific generation makes it function, in contemporary Polish internet culture, as a shorthand for a particular kind of older Polish femininity.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Kitsch sentimentality, nostalgia for socialist-era Poland, communal warmth
